group: NumericIndicator.crossedOver(Number) - basic functionality and edge cases

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(2) == true (delegate crosses from <=5 to >5 at index 2)
cases.description: Verify that crossedOver(Number) creates a CrossedUpIndicatorRule that becomes satisfied when the underlying NumericIndicator value crosses above the constant 5. The series is set up so the value is 4 at index 1 and 6 at index 2.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(3) == true (cross from <=-3 to >-3)
cases.description: Test crossing over a negative constant. The series values are -4 at index 2 and -2 at index 3, causing the rule to be satisfied at index 3.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(1) == false, rule.isSatisfied(2) == true
cases.description: Crossing over zero. The series is -1 at index 0, -0.5 at index 1, and 0.2 at index 2, so the rule should become satisfied only at index 2.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(any index) == false
cases.description: Constant far above any series value – the rule should never be satisfied because the indicator never crosses the constant.
Passing a null Number should result in a NullPointerException, as the method attempts to create a constant indicator from the argument.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException or Rule that is never satisfied
cases.description: NaN is not a valid constant for comparison; the implementation should either reject it with an exception or produce a rule that never becomes satisfied.

group: NumericIndicator.crossedOver(Number) - additional edge and type cases

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(any index) == false (indicator values are always > -1000, so no crossing from <= to > can occur)
cases.description: Constant far below the minimum series value. The underlying NumericIndicator never goes from <= -1000 to > -1000, therefore the rule must never be satisfied.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(2) == true, rule.isSatisfied(1) == false
cases.description: Series values: 3.5 at index 0, 3.4 at index 1, 3.6 at index 2. The constant equals the first value; the rule should become satisfied only when the value crosses from ≤ 3.5 (index 1) to > 3.5 (index 2).

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(any index) == false (a finite indicator can never cross above positive infinity)
cases.description: Using Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY as the constant. No crossing can ever happen, so the rule must always be unsatisfied.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(any index) == false (the indicator is always > -∞, thus never crosses from <= to >)
cases.description: Using Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY as the constant. Since every numeric value is greater than -∞, there is no crossing event.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(any index) == false (series values stay well below Integer.MAX_VALUE)
cases.description: Constant set to Integer.MAX_VALUE. The series values are far lower, so the rule never becomes satisfied.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(1) == true, rule.isSatisfied(2) == false, rule.isSatisfied(3) == true (multiple up‑crossings)
cases.description: Series values: -1 at index 0, 0.1 at index 1 (first up‑cross), -0.2 at index 2, 0.5 at index 3 (second up‑cross). The rule should be satisfied only at the indices where the crossing from ≤ 0 to > 0 occurs.

cases.expected: Rule instance of CrossedUpIndicatorRule; rule.isSatisfied(1) == true
cases.description: Constant supplied as a Long (5L). Series values: 4 at index 0, 6 at index 1. Confirms that the method correctly handles non‑Double Number types.
Passing Double.NaN should cause the method to reject the constant and throw IllegalArgumentException, as NaN is not a valid numeric value for comparison.
Passing Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY should trigger an IllegalArgumentException because an infinite constant cannot be represented as a finite Num for rule evaluation.
Passing Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY should trigger an IllegalArgumentException for the same reason as positive infinity – infinite values are not allowed in constant indicators.
